title: The Butterfly Defects: Tracing Cooperation in LLM Agent Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.32726v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate as interconnected agents, a fundamental question emerges: does individual cooperation translate into collective cooperation? We investigate this question through the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD), moving from dyadic interactions to homogeneous and heterogeneous networks of open-weight LLMs. Our findings reveal that cooperation is highly sensitive to model composition and seemingly minor linguistic changes. Models that cooperate with identical peers can shift toward defection in mixed populations. A simple uncertainty cue can increase or decrease cooperation, redistribute costs, and affect unexposed agents several hops away. Even reversing action-label order can dramatically alter behavior, with uncertainty framing sometimes amplifying this sensitivity. translated_title: 蝴蝶缺陷：追踪大语言模型智能体网络中的合作行为
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地以相互连接的智能体形式运作，一个根本性问题浮现出来：个体层面的合作是否会转化为集体层面的合作？我们通过迭代囚徒困境（IPD）对这一问题进行研究，从双主体交互扩展到由开放权重LLM构成的同质与异质网络。我们的发现表明，合作行为对模型组成以及看似微小的语言变化高度敏感。与完全相同的同伴交互时表现合作的模型，在混合群体中可能转向背叛。一个简单的不确定性提示可以增加或减少合作、重新分配成本，并影响数跳之外未直接暴露的智能体。甚至反转动作标签的顺序也会显著改变行为，而不确定性框架有时会进一步放大这种敏感性。这些发现共同挑战了将合作视为稳定的模型级属性的观念，揭示了策略性行为的动态特性。
tldr: 该论文通过迭代囚徒困境实验发现，大语言模型智能体网络中的合作行为高度依赖模型组成与微小的语言变化（如不确定性提示、动作标签顺序），从而挑战了合作是稳定模型级属性的观念。
en_tdlr: This paper shows through Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma experiments that cooperation in LLM agent networks is highly sensitive to model composition and minor linguistic changes (such as uncertainty cues and action-label ordering), challenging the notion of cooperation as a stable model-level property.
